slug: 2026-01-10 Cameroon - First digital birth certificate in the North-West and South-West regions (UNDP)

facts.fact: On 7 January 2026 a birth certificate collected at Limbe I Council became the first civil certificate issued through a fully digitalised civil registration system in the North-West and South-West regions, per UNDP Cameroon.
facts.system: digitalised civil registration system (UNDP project councils)

facts.fact: The first certificate issued through the digitalised system at Limbe I Council on 7 January 2026 was a birth certificate, per UNDP Cameroon.
facts.system: digitalised civil registration system (UNDP project councils)

facts.fact: UNDP Cameroon's project covers ten municipalities: Maroua III, Koza, Mindif, Meri, Mora, Limbe I, Buea, Tiko, Bamenda III and Bamenda City Council; the document says only Limbe I had issued a certificate by 7 January 2026 in the two anglophone regions, and gives no national total.
facts.system: digitalised civil registration system (UNDP project councils)

facts.fact: The ten municipalities are covered by UNDP Cameroon's Denmark-funded project 'Contributing to Social Cohesion Efforts in the Far-North, North-West and South-West Regions'.
facts.system: digitalised civil registration system (UNDP project councils)

systems.system: digitalised civil registration system (UNDP project councils)
systems.owner: UNDP Cameroon project, under the BUNEC-led reform
systems.tiers: ten municipalities in the Far North, North-West and South-West; first certificate at Limbe I on 7 January 2026

note: The held text is a two-paragraph summary of the UNDP story, not its full body.
